subject.title: Guard Telegram and iMessage dispatch against fleet loops

question: Should Telegram/iMessage loop suppression be implemented as in-repo channel/turn admission, or may shared core dispatch call a host-local `fleet-loop-guard` binary with message and session data?
rationale: This changes a core dispatch security boundary and owner boundary; automation cannot decide whether OpenClaw should trust and document an external executable path for inbound message suppression.

options.title: Require In-Repo Admission Guard
options.body: Move the guard into channel-owned or shared turn admission before session record and dispatch, reusing the existing bot-loop protection contract where possible.

options.title: Accept Host-Local Helper Contract
options.body: Allow the external binary only after maintainers document installation, versioning, timeout, data-sharing, and operator security expectations.

options.title: Pause This Branch
options.body: Pause or close this branch if the fleet-loop scenario should be handled by a narrower Telegram/iMessage design item instead of shared dispatch.

recommendation.title: Require In-Repo Admission Guard
recommendation.body: Move the guard into channel-owned or shared turn admission before session record and dispatch, reusing the existing bot-loop protection contract where possible.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice intersects the generic bot-loop guard and provider-dispatcher seams that `steipete` recently introduced or maintained.
